correctness.rationale: For the real anchored Lipschitz polytope, inequalities |T|<=t, |Yi|<=1 and |Yi-T|<=1 imply independent leaf fibers centered T/2 and length 2-|T|; pairwise leaf inequalities follow automatically. Fubini proves volume 2H_m and disintegration. Conditional moments give v=E T^2, w=E(2-|T|)^2/12, determinant v*w^m via unit-determinant shear, and the stated two remaining covariance eigenvalues. Scale S=mT: dominated exponential envelopes give uniform/truncated/full two-sided Laplace crossover, whereas sum of independent centered leaf uniforms has Gaussian CLT and asymptotic independence by Slutsky. Universal bounds for H_m and v for alpha=min(t,1/m) with w->1/3 imply L->1/sqrt(12) even exponentially small t. Independently recomputed 35 exact rational (m,t) second-moment cases; finite checks corroborate rather than prove uniform m theorem.

value.rationale: Metric Lipschitz balls and their uniform interior laws are natural affine/Banach-space objects. The exact covariance and isotropic constant in a varying weight parameter, especially the sharp dimension-dependent Laplace/Gaussian independence crossover, are motivated quantitative invariants not a routine corollary of faces, volume products, or an enclosing ellipsoid. The scalar volume by itself is elementary and not isolated as a novelty claim.
